script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for November 6. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Cold muscles tear.  Cold engines stall.  You can't go from zero to maximum instantly—bodies and machines both need warm-up.

Warm-up is gradual transition—moving from resting state to performance state step by step. Each stage prepares the next. Rushing the transition invites problems. Warm-up activates systems: blood flows, muscles activate, joints lubricate, focus sharpens.  It's not just muscles—it's the whole system preparing for demands.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Transitions matter.  Jumping from rest to peak performance invites failure.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Transition Audit - Where Do You Skip Warm-Up?.

Here's your activity: Where do you jump straight into demands without warm-up—exercise, work, difficult conversations? What preparation phase could you add? Design a warm-up routine for a demanding activity in your life. This helps you identify areas needing better preparation phases.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about preparing your body can be applied to transition audit - where do you skip warm-up?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
